key_insight: EdgeDAM shows that a lightweight, distractor-aware memory design that avoids costly mask prediction and heavy attention lets single-object trackers run in real time on mobile/edge devices without large overhead.
problem_solved: Reduces the computational and memory overhead of segmentation-based distractor-aware trackers, enabling accurate, continuous single-object tracking under occlusion and distractors on resource-constrained mobile hardware.
method: Replace mask-driven memory updates with a compact, bounding-box-level distractor-aware memory that stores and updates discriminative features rather than full segmentation masks.
Use sparse/efficient attention and feature compression (hardware-aware ops, quantization-friendly blocks) to minimize runtime and memory access during recall and update.
Integrate a mobile-optimized backbone and engineering optimizations (pruning/quantization and edge runtime tooling) to ensure real-time inference on phones.
impact: Makes robust single-object tracking practical on edge devices, unlocking real-time AR, mobile robotics, and surveillance applications while lowering energy and latency constraints for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: streamlined pipeline comparing segmentation-based memory (heavy) vs EdgeDAM's compact memory (light) with callouts for key modules.
Bar chart: latency and compute (FLOPs or MACs) vs tracking accuracy for prior methods vs EdgeDAM to highlight efficiency gains.
Sequence strip: sample video frames showing stable tracking through occlusion and distractors with bounding-box overlays.
Device mockup: smartphone icon with FPS and power/latency indicators to emphasize real-time edge deployment.
paper_title: EdgeDAM: Real-time Object Tracking for Mobile Devices
paper_authors: Syed Muhammad Raza, Syed Murtaza Hussain Abidi, Khawar Islam, Muhammad Ibrahim, Ajmal Saeed Mian
